text: Astronomers use powerful telescopes to study the universe and its many wonders. Telescopes allow us to observe distant objects, like nebulae, which are vast interstellar clouds of gas and dust. These nebulae are often the birthplace of new stars. By studying the light from these nebulae, scientists can learn about the conditions and materials present in the universe billions of years ago. This knowledge helps us understand the formation and evolution of stars and galaxies.
